thread.title: Netflix (NFLX) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Netflix (NFLX) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Shutterstock photo
Netflix ( NFLX ) will report third quarter fiscal 2018 earnings results after the closing bell Tuesday. The results will be the first among its FAANG peers — Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), which have all suffered during the recent tech selloff.
For Netflix, however, the Internet movie streaming giant will look to bounce back after Q2 subscriber additions for both domestic and international, fell short of Wall Street expectations. Netflix shares fell sharply as a result. And despite being up more than 70% year to date, the shares are still much lower from their mid-summer high of nearly $419. But analysts remain positive that the Q2 disappointment, attributed to World Cup euphoria, was not the beginning of a trend.
For the quarter that ended September, Wall Street expects Netflix to earn 68 cents per share on revenue of $4.01 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earning were 29 cents per share on $2.98 billion in revenue. For the full year, ending December, earnings are projected to rise 116% to $2.70 per share, while full-year revenue of $15.85 billion would mark an increase of 35.5% year over year.
Beyond the top- and bottom line numbers, the company’s subscriber growth totals, which often drives the share price, will be the key metric that sets the tone as to whether the Q2 miss was really just an aberration. Last quarter’s new sub total of 5.15 million was not only well below the 6.2 million it guided for, it was also down from the 7.41 million it netted in the first quarter. The miss sent the stock falling to $316 mid-August from its all-time high of $423 in August.
Netflix CEO Reed Hastings assured analysts that the sub miss was merely a blip on the broader spectrum, calling it “some lumpiness in the business.” Wall Street isn’t worried, either.
“We view Netflix as a pioneer in online streaming, with further expected growth in subs in the U.S. and expectation for long-term sub growth internationally in existing and new markets,” noted John Blackledge, analyst at Cowen & Co.
For the quarter, Wall Street expects 5.32 million net subscriber additions, which would be flat on a year-over-year basis. That figure, however, is above the company’s forecast of 5.0 million. Of which, 65 thousand is expected the U.S., while 4.35 million is expected internationally. Competition from Google’s YouTube and Amazon’s Prime Video heightens the importance of Netflix’s growth in international markets this quarter and going forward. Having invested significantly in its international expansion , Netflix understands this.
All told, while Netflix may begin to see slower U.S. sub growth , the notion of “peak subscriber” won’t (or shouldn’t) enter the conversation, given the opportunity it still has internationally. And the fact that its full year profits are expected to grow at over almost 120% underscores its pricing power. And until there are clearer signs of slowing subscriber growth, staying long Netflix stock remains the best strategy.
